name: Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus
description: A self-contained corporate arcology occupying a 40-block footprint in the mid-city corridor, Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus was constructed over a fifteen-year period by the Vantage Meridian Group — a multi-sector conglomerate spanning biotech, private security, data brokerage, and consumer electronics. From the outside, the Campus presents a gleaming wall of climate-managed glass towers connected by elevated skyways and manicured green terraces visible from street level, a deliberate architectural statement about the separation between corporate life and the city beyond its perimeter.

sights: Immaculate white and glass facades with no visible seams or weathering
Color-coded employee tiers moving through skyways in controlled flows
Ornamental trees in climate-regulated planters — some species extinct in the wild
Security checkpoints with biometric arches every 200 meters
Promotional holographic displays cycling through corporate achievement metrics
sounds: Carefully curated ambient soundscapes piped through outdoor speakers
The near-silence of suppressed urban noise inside the perimeter
Corporate announcements delivered in calm, gender-neutral synthesized voices
The soft whir of internal transit pods on elevated rails
Muffled city noise from beyond the acoustic barriers — a constant reminder of the outside
smells: Artificial fresh air pumped through filtered ventilation — faintly floral and entirely synthetic
Coffee and meal-service aromas timed to shift cycles
Antiseptic cleanliness in the lower-tier corridors
A faint chemical undertone near the biotech research wings that staff have stopped noticing
atmosphere.feel: Oppressively calm. The Campus is engineered to produce contentment, and it succeeds in a way that feels slightly wrong upon reflection. Everything is convenient, nothing is spontaneous, and the comfort has the texture of a soft cage.

demographics: Roughly 40,000 on-campus employees ranging from Tier 1 contract laborers (maintenance, food service, security) to Tier 5 executive staff. A significant population of long-term residents who have not left the Campus perimeter in months or years. No unofficial residents; all individuals are registered, monitored, and categorized.
economy: Entirely internal and corporate-controlled. Employees are compensated in a mix of city-currency and Campus credits, the latter only redeemable within Vantage Meridian's ecosystem. Housing, food, medical care, and entertainment are all Campus-provided, creating deliberate dependency. The Campus generates enormous revenue externally through its data brokerage and biotech divisions.
power_structure: The Vantage Meridian Group's Board of Directors governs absolutely within Campus boundaries, which carry special economic zone status exempting them from significant city regulation. Day-to-day administration is managed by the Operations Directorate, with the Internal Security Division (ISD) functioning as a private police force with broad authority. Employee councils exist on paper but hold no real power.
dangers: ISD officers operate with near-total impunity within Campus boundaries
Behavioral monitoring is pervasive — dissent, even private, carries career and physical risk
Employees who attempt to leave contracts early are pursued through debt and legal mechanisms
The biotech research division has produced several contained incidents that official records do not acknowledge
Corporate espionage operations from rival entities sometimes catch bystanders in the crossfire
Psychological dependency on Campus infrastructure is deliberately cultivated and difficult to break
opportunities: Access to cutting-edge biotech research and proprietary data systems for those who can infiltrate
Disgruntled employees at every tier represent potential informants or allies
The Campus's internal logistics network can be exploited for smuggling if the right contacts are established
Vantage Meridian's data brokerage division holds files on nearly every significant figure in GLMZ
Contract security work through ISD provides access to restricted areas and corporate intelligence
story_hooks: A Tier 3 researcher has been attempting to smuggle out evidence of undisclosed human trial data and needs a secure extraction
Someone is killing ISD officers inside the Campus perimeter using methods that bypass all surveillance — and the Campus cannot admit it needs outside help
A new Vantage Meridian product scheduled for city-wide release contains something that wasn't in the published specifications
An executive has gone into voluntary isolation in their Campus apartment and stopped responding to all communications — their division has continued to function normally without them
A Tier 1 maintenance worker has accidentally discovered access to a server room that doesn't appear on any Campus schematic
frequented_by: Corporate journalists on controlled press access
Rival corporate intelligence operatives in deep cover
City officials on scheduled liaison visits

notable_locations.name: The Atrium
notable_locations.description: The Campus's central public-facing space — a vast glass-roofed hall containing restaurants, retail, and recreational facilities theoretically open to the public, though entry requires biometric registration. It functions as a showroom for the Vantage Meridian lifestyle and as the primary mixing zone where different employee tiers interact under calculated informality.

notable_locations.name: Research Tower Seven
notable_locations.description: The only Campus tower with no external windows above the third floor. Officially housing advanced materials research, Tower Seven has a separate security clearance system, its own power grid, and air handling that does not connect to the rest of the Campus. Long-term Campus employees know not to ask about it.

notable_locations.name: The Perimeter Corridor
notable_locations.description: The narrow zone between the Campus boundary wall and the adjacent city streets — technically outside Campus jurisdiction but informally patrolled by ISD. It has become a grey-zone gathering spot for Campus workers on break, small-time vendors catering to them, and the occasional person waiting to make contact with someone inside without triggering a formal visit.
